To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multivitamin/minerals did not affect standardized academic performance in elementary children.
multivitamin mineral supplementation did not improve academic performance in school age children.
the daily consumption of an in school administered standard multivitamin/minerals did not affect standardized academic performance in third through sixth grade children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of a multivitamin/mineraldaily supplementation on academic performance in school age children.
the effects of multivitamin/ mineral (MVM) supplementation on the academic performance of inner city elementary school children.
the effect of multimineral/multivitamin supplementation on the academic performance of inner city children in grades 3 to 6 in parochial schools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consumption of a daily multivitamin/ mineral supplement by school aged inner city children does not affect their standardized assessment of academic performances.
there is insufficient evidence to recommend or discourage the daily use of a multivitamin/mineraldietary supplement for the purpose of enhancing academic performance in school aged children.
there is no evidence that daily consumption of a standard multivitamin/minerals supplement by school aged children improves academic performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no evidence that multivitamin and mineral supplementation improves school performance in children, but there is also no evidence that they harm it.
MVM supplementation did not affect academic performance in elementary aged children.
there is not a benefit of MVM supplementation on school performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multivitamin/minerals are unlikely to have a significant effect on school performance in children.
there is no benefit to taking multivitamins for children.
the use of MVM supplements in school aged children should not be based upon the assumption that it will improve school performance.
